title: 12 State Titles, One Secret — Building Teams Kids Never Want to Quit

guestDetails.name: John Weaver
guestDetails.role: 21-year high school coach — 9 state track titles, 3 straight football championships — Athletic Director at Madison-Ridgeland Academy

hook: Nine state track titles. Three straight football championships. Coach John Weaver says the secret behind all of it has nothing to do with talent.
description: Coach Philip Short sits down with Coach John Weaver — a 21-year high school coach and the new athletic director at Madison-Ridgeland Academy — to break down what actually builds championship programs: recruiting the hallways instead of waiting on talent, the handwritten notes he gave players before every game, the undefeated COVID season built on brotherhood, and the one cue that won a state pole vault championship. Plus the stuff every parent needs to hear — the five words your child needs after every game, why kids quit sports that stop being fun, and how to avoid becoming a helicopter (or lawnmower) parent.

title: Raising Strong Kids — Fitness, Faith, and Family

guestDetails.name: Michael McElroy
guestDetails.role: Strength and athletic performance coach · former CrossFit Games competitor · trains athletes out of his home gym in Madison, MS

guestDetails.name: Reagan McElroy
guestDetails.role: Group fitness coach at Burn Boot Camp · RN · CrossFit and HYROX competitor

hook: A CrossFit-HYROX couple, four homeschooled kids, and a gym in their barn — how do you raise strong, healthy kids without burning them out?
description: Stone Blanton sits down with Michael and Reagan McElroy — a husband-and-wife fitness team right here in Madison who built a gym in their barn and homeschool their four kids. They unpack how to raise active kids without forcing it, why structured training too early kills the joy, the case for loaded mobility and end-range strength as the real key to keeping athletes healthy, the danger of year-round single-sport specialization, screen time, and the family rule they live by: faith, family, fitness — in that order. A practical conversation for any parent trying to model the discipline they want their kids to inherit.

title: How MSI Started — From a Backyard to Notre Dame

guestDetails.name: Mike Frascogna III
guestDetails.role: Founder of Mississippi Speed Instruction (est. 1993) · former Notre Dame walk-on wide receiver under Lou Holtz · partner at Frascogna Law Group in Jackson, MS · MBA, Millsaps College · JD, Mississippi College School of Law

hook: A tiny ad in the back of a coaching magazine, prototype speed gear in a garage, and a 5'8" walk-on who shocked Notre Dame's strength coach.
description: Coach Philip Short sits down with the founder of Mississippi Speed Instruction himself — Mike Frascogna III. The full origin story: a 1980s speed camp that almost didn't happen in Mississippi, prototype training equipment that sat in his parents' garage for years, the summer Mike trained alone behind his house six days a week, and the walk-on tryout at Notre Dame where his 40 time alone got him on the team. Plus Lou Holtz's three rules for life ('do what is right, do it to the best of your ability, show people you care'), how MSI started in 1993 while Mike was still a student, the Speed City video library (once the largest collection of SAQ training videos in the world), and how training his son Rocco's flag football team — the Raptors — brought him back to coaching the next generation.

title: From MRA to the NFL — What It Actually Takes

guestDetails.name: Stone Blanton
guestDetails.role: Linebacker · Madison Ridgeland Academy graduate · four-star recruit and Butkus Award semifinalist · South Carolina (2 seasons) → Mississippi State (125 tackles, 2nd in the SEC, all-SEC 2024) · signed with the San Francisco 49ers as an undrafted free agent (May 2025) · Tennessee Titans minicamp trial

hook: How a Madison kid took his speed all the way to the NFL — film, faith, and being where your feet are.
description: Coach Philip Short sits down with Stone Blanton — Madison Ridgeland Academy graduate, four-star linebacker, and Butkus Award semifinalist. After two seasons at South Carolina, Stone came home to Mississippi State, where his 2024 season (125 tackles, second in the SEC, ninth in the nation, all-SEC honors) put him on the NFL radar. In May 2025 he signed with the San Francisco 49ers as an undrafted free agent. Stone and Philip dig into why playing every sport as a kid built the foundation, how the Coach Adams workouts at MRA prepared him for the SEC, the mental edge he built sleeping in the South Carolina facility for two weeks of fall camp, the brutal revolving door of NFL cuts, and the BCD rule he carries with him (no Blame, no Complaining, no Defending) — plus what it really means to 'be where your feet are.'

title: Only 6% of Kids Make It to College Sports — Here's What Most Parents Get Wrong

guestDetails.name: George Adams
guestDetails.role: Head Athletic Performance Coach, Madison-Ridgeland Academy · 8 state championships · former coach at Minnesota Vikings and University of Georgia

hook: Only 6% of high school athletes ever play college sports. So why train like the goal is D1?
description: Coach Philip Short sits down with George Adams — Head Athletic Performance Coach at Madison-Ridgeland Academy, an eight-time state champion, and a former coach at the Minnesota Vikings and the University of Georgia. They dig into why only 6% of high school athletes ever play college sports, why over-structured 'specialized' training is quietly burning kids out, and why free play builds better athletes than running cone to cone. George breaks down the three things he demands from every athlete — attitude, effort, and consistency — and why quality reps, real sleep, and good nutrition matter far more than chasing a D1 dream.

title: What SEC-Level Speed Actually Takes (What 99% of Parents Miss)

guestDetails.name: Lauren Stratton
guestDetails.role: Former Mississippi State Soccer · Madison Academy girls' soccer coach

guestDetails.name: Kat Stratton
guestDetails.role: Assistant Coach, Mississippi State Women's Soccer · 2024 SEC Champion · former Alabama

hook: Most parents think their kid is either born fast — or they're not. Two coaches with SEC playing experience break down what actually builds great athletes.
description: Coach Lauren Stratton played at Mississippi State. Coach Kat Stratton played at Alabama and is now an assistant coach at Mississippi State, where her staff won the 2024 SEC Championship. They sit down with Coach Philip Short to break down what really builds great athletes from age 7 all the way to college — and what most parents are missing. We cover specialization, the weight room myth for girls, why fatigue beats skill, how to make practice harder than the game, and the one thing every parent should do differently for their daughter.
